message.content:
Write BDD spec files (spex) for story 838 "Track time and per-job pay in one system" in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm (Phoenix app, module CleanerCrm).

REQUIRED READING first, in this order:
1. mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__read_knowledge with path "bdd/spex/writing_a_spex.md"
2. mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__read_knowledge with path "bdd/spex/boundaries.md"
3. Local file .code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/index.md
4. test/support/cleaner_crm_spex_case.ex
5. test/support/fixtures/cleaner_crm_spex_fixtures.ex — note existing fixtures: user/account/client/job/cleaner fixtures, log_in_user
6. test/support/shared_givens.ex
7. Any spec file under test/spex/836_*/ as a style reference

Then call mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__get_story_gherkin with story_id 838 and encode those scenarios faithfully into the spex files.

Write ONE file per criterion at EXACTLY these paths (all in the same directory test/spex/838_track_time_and_per-job_pay_in_one_system/):
- criterion_7121_cleaner_clocks_in_and_out_of_an_assigned_job_spex.exs
- criterion_7123_cleaner_tries_to_clock_in_on_a_job_not_assigned_to_them_spex.exs
- criterion_7125_hourly_job_pays_rate_times_worked_hours_spex.exs
- criterion_7128_per-job_piece_rate_pays_a_fixed_amount_regardless_of_time_spex.exs
- criterion_7130_running_pay-period_total_builds_as_jobs_complete_spex.exs
- criterion_7134_owner_exports_a_completed_pay_period_to_csv_spex.exs
- criterion_7137_cleaner_forgets_to_clock_out_spex.exs
- criterion_7140_export_blocked_while_an_unresolved_time_entry_remains_spex.exs

Strict rules:
- `use CleanerCrmSpex.Case` in every file.
- given_/when_/then_ helper functions must return {:ok, context}.
- Surfaces to encode: cleaner clocks in/out of a job via FieldLive.Job (~p"/field/jobs/:id"); owner reviews timesheet and exports CSV via TimesheetLive (~p"/timesheets"). These routes/LiveViews do NOT exist yet — the specs are expected to fail red; that failure is the deliverable, do not work around it.
- Money renders as a string in the form "$X.XX" (integer-cents ADR — do not use floats for money).
- NO if/case/cond control flow inside spex files.
- NO direct calls to CleanerCrm.<Context>, Repo, File, Port, apply/1, or send/2,3 from spex files.
- NO skip/pending tags on any test.
- NO mocks/mocking libraries.
- If you need a new fixture that delegates to a context/function that doesn't exist yet, add that fixture to cleaner_crm_spex_fixtures.ex and add the target module to the existing `@compile {:no_warn_undefined, [...]}` list there (extend the list, don't replace it).
- Do NOT call mcp__plugin_codemyspec_local__start_task or evaluate_task for this work.

Verification steps for every file you write:
1. `elixir -e 'Code.string_to_quoted!(File.read!("<path>"))'` must succeed (parses cleanly) for each of the 8 files.
2. `mix credo 2>&1 | grep test/spex` must return empty (no credo findings under test/spex).

Report back (to me, the orchestrating agent) a final summary under 120 words: list of files written and pass/fail status of the parse + credo checks. Do not include lengthy code dumps.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [CleanerCrm.Clients, CleanerCrm.Scheduling, CleanerCrm.Quality, CleanerCrm.Billing]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end
end

1	# BDD Spec Plan — Cleaner CRM
2	
3	How BDD specs work in *this* project. The framework docs
4	(`philosophy.md`, `boundaries.md`, `writing_a_spex.md` in the harness
5	knowledge base) cover the generic rules; this file names the concrete
6	surfaces, fixtures, and anti-patterns for Cleaner CRM.
7	
8	## Public surfaces a spec may drive
9	
10	Specs act through LiveView routes (via `Phoenix.LiveViewTest`) and the
11	public controllers. Concretely:
12	
13	**Office/admin side (owner persona):**
14	- `CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.*` — `/clients`, client + property + access management (story 832)
15	- `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Board` — `/schedule`, weekly dispatch board (833, 834, 846)
16	- `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.*` — `/quotes`, quote builder (835)
17	- `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.*` — `/invoices` (836)
18	- `CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive` — reminder settings + delivery log (837)
19	- `CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetLive` — time review + payroll export (838)
20	- `CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.*` — job review + scorecards (839)
21	- `CleanerCrmWeb.AuditLive` — audit trail (840)
22	
23	**Cleaner field side (cleaner persona):**
24	- `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Today` — day view + change alerts (841, 843)
25	- `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job` — checklist, photos, clock in/out, incident reports (842, 844, 845)
26	
27	**Public (unauthenticated) surfaces:**
28	- `CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController` — payment-link pages (836)
29	- `CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderController` — reminder confirm/reschedule links (837)
30	- Auth: `/users/register`, `/users/log-in` LiveViews (generated)
31	
32	## Fixture inventory (`CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`)
33	
34	- `user_fixture/1` — confirmed user (owner/office/cleaner depending on attrs)
35	- `unconfirmed_user_fixture/1` — pre-confirmation user for auth specs
36	- `user_scope_fixture/0,1` — scope wrapping a user, for seeding deeper state
37	- `valid_user_password/0`, `set_password/1` — password login in specs
38	- `account_fixture/2` — a company (tenant) owned by the given scope
39	
40	Grow this list only when a spec's `given_` needs state whose creation
41	flow is covered by another spec. Every addition is a sanctioned bypass.
42	
43	## Legal observable surfaces in `then_`
44	
45	- LiveView render assertions: `assert render(view) =~ "Job scheduled"`
46	- LiveView navigation: `assert_patch/2`, `assert_redirect/2`
47	- Flash content via rendered layout
48	- Controller responses: `html_response(conn, 200)`, redirects on payment/reminder links
49	- Email delivery via `Swoosh.TestAssertions` (reminder + invitation emails)
50	- NOT legal: asserting on Repo rows, context return values, or PubSub
51	  messages via direct `assert_receive` on internals — observe what a
52	  user (or webhook peer) can observe.
53	
54	## Project-specific anti-patterns
55	
56	- Do not seed `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` jobs in `given_` by calling the
57	  context — the covered creation flow is the ScheduleLive board / plan
58	  form. If a spec needs "a scheduled job" as a precondition, either
59	  drive the UI in `given_` steps or add a sanctioned fixture here first.
60	- Do not flip `Notification` acknowledgment state directly — the whole
61	  point of story 843 is the acknowledgment round-trip through
62	  `FieldLive.Today`.
63	- Do not stub time by editing rows; recurrence/conflict scenarios pin
64	  wall-clock via plan dates chosen in the future.
65	- External HTTP (Stripe, Twilio, Resend, S3) is always cassette- or
66	  adapter-faked; a spec must never hit a live API.
67

- `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.*` — `/quotes`, quote builder (835)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.*` — `/invoices` (836)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive` — reminder settings + delivery log (837)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetLive` — time review + payroll export (838)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.*` — job review + scorecards (839)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.AuditLive` — audit trail (840)

**Cleaner field side (cleaner persona):**
- `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Today` — day view + change alerts (841, 843)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job` — checklist, photos, clock in/out, incident reports (842, 844, 845)

**Public (unauthenticated) surfaces:**
- `CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController` — payment-link pages (836)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderController` — reminder confirm/reschedule links (837)
- Auth: `/users/register`, `/users/log-in` LiveViews (generated)

## Fixture inventory (`CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`)

- `user_fixture/1` — confirmed user (owner/office/cleaner depending on attrs)
- `unconfirmed_user_fixture/1` — pre-confirmation user for auth specs
- `user_scope_fixture/0,1` — scope wrapping a user, for seeding deeper state
- `valid_user_password/0`, `set_password/1` — password login in specs
- `account_fixture/2` — a company (tenant) owned by the given scope

Grow this list only when a spec's `given_` needs state whose creation
flow is covered by another spec. Every addition is a sanctioned bypass.

## Legal observable surfaces in `then_`

- LiveView render assertions: `assert render(view) =~ "Job scheduled"`
- LiveView navigation: `assert_patch/2`, `assert_redirect/2`
- Flash content via rendered layout
- Controller responses: `html_response(conn, 200)`, redirects on payment/reminder links
- Email delivery via `Swoosh.TestAssertions` (reminder + invitation emails)
- NOT legal: asserting on Repo rows, context return values, or PubSub
  messages via direct `assert_receive` on internals — observe what a
  user (or webhook peer) can observe.

## Project-specific anti-patterns

- Do not seed `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` jobs in `given_` by calling the
  context — the covered creation flow is the ScheduleLive board / plan
  form. If a spec needs "a scheduled job" as a precondition, either
  drive the UI in `given_` steps or add a sanctioned fixture here first.
- Do not flip `Notification` acknowledgment state directly — the whole
  point of story 843 is the acknowledgment round-trip through
  `FieldLive.Today`.
- Do not stub time by editing rows; recurrence/conflict scenarios pin
  wall-clock via plan dates chosen in the future.
- External HTTP (Stripe, Twilio, Resend, S3) is always cassette- or
  adapter-faked; a spec must never hit a live API.

1	defmodule CodeMySpec.Check.Warning.NoControlFlowInTests do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Credo check that forbids imperative control flow (`case`, `if`, `unless`,
4	  `cond`, `try`) inside test files (`_test.exs`) and BDD spec files
5	  (`_spex.exs`). See the `:check` explanation for rationale.
6	  """
7	
8	  use Credo.Check,
9	    id: "CMS0003",
10	    base_priority: :high,
11	    category: :warning,
12	    explanations: [
13	      check: """
14	      Imperative control flow (`case`, `if`, `cond`, `try/rescue`) is not allowed
15	      in test files (`_test.exs`) or BDD spec files (`_spex.exs`).
16	
17	      Tests and scenarios should be declarative — straight-line setup +
18	      observation + assertion. Control flow in a test hides what's actually
19	      being asserted, makes failure output harder to read, and signals that
20	      the fixture isn't doing its job (the test is defending against shapes
21	      the setup should guarantee).
22	
23	      Replace with:
24	      - Pattern-matching `=` for destructuring (`{:ok, value} = result`).
25	      - `assert match?(pattern, value)` for shape assertions.
26	      - Multi-clause helper functions (`defp handle(:ok, ...)` + `defp handle(:error, ...)`).
27	      - Tightening the fixture so the assertion can rely on a known shape.
28	      - For scenarios with conditional setup, split into separate tests/scenarios.
29	
30	      Pattern matching in function heads and `with` clauses is fine —
31	      that's destructuring, not control flow. The forbidden constructs
32	      are imperative branching inside the test/scenario body.
33	      """
34	    ]
35	
36	  @doc false
37	  @impl true
38	  def run(%SourceFile{filename: filename} = source_file, params) do
39	    if test_or_spex?(filename) do
40	      ctx = Context.build(source_file, params, __MODULE__)
41	      result = Credo.Code.prewalk(source_file, &walk/2, ctx)
42	      result.issues
43	    else
44	      []
45	    end
46	  end
47	
48	  defp test_or_spex?(filename) do
49	    String.ends_with?(filename, "_test.exs") or String.ends_with?(filename, "_spex.exs")
50	  end
51	
52	  defp walk({:case, meta, _} = ast, ctx) do
53	    {ast, put_issue(ctx, issue_for(ctx, meta, "case"))}
54	  end
55	
56	  defp walk({:if, meta, _} = ast, ctx) do
57	    {ast, put_issue(ctx, issue_for(ctx, meta, "if"))}
58	  end
59	
60	  defp walk({:unless, meta, _} = ast, ctx) do
61	    {ast, put_issue(ctx, issue_for(ctx, meta, "unless"))}
62	  end
63	
64	  defp walk({:cond, meta, _} = ast, ctx) do
65	    {ast, put_issue(ctx, issue_for(ctx, meta, "cond"))}
66	  end
67	
68	  defp walk({:try, meta, _} = ast, ctx) do
69	    {ast, put_issue(ctx, issue_for(ctx, meta, "try"))}
70	  end
71	
72	  defp walk(ast, ctx) do
73	    {ast, ctx}
74	  end
75	
76	  defp issue_for(issue_meta, meta, construct) do
77	    format_issue(
78	      issue_meta,
79	      message:
80	        "Imperative `#{construct}` is not allowed in _test.exs / _spex.exs files. " <>
81	          "Use pattern matching, multi-clause helpers, or split into separate tests/scenarios.",
82	      trigger: construct,
83	      line_no: meta[:line],
84	      column: meta[:column]
85	    )
86	  end
87	end
88

      in test files (`_test.exs`) or BDD spec files (`_spex.exs`).

      Tests and scenarios should be declarative — straight-line setup +
      observation + assertion. Control flow in a test hides what's actually
      being asserted, makes failure output harder to read, and signals that
      the fixture isn't doing its job (the test is defending against shapes
      the setup should guarantee).

      Replace with:
      - Pattern-matching `=` for destructuring (`{:ok, value} = result`).
      - `assert match?(pattern, value)` for shape assertions.
      - Multi-clause helper functions (`defp handle(:ok, ...)` + `defp handle(:error, ...)`).
      - Tightening the fixture so the assertion can rely on a known shape.
      - For scenarios with conditional setup, split into separate tests/scenarios.

      Pattern matching in function heads and `with` clauses is fine —
      that's destructuring, not control flow. The forbidden constructs
      are imperative branching inside the test/scenario body.
      """
    ]

  @doc false
  @impl true
  def run(%SourceFile{filename: filename} = source_file, params) do
    if test_or_spex?(filename) do
      ctx = Context.build(source_file, params, __MODULE__)
      result = Credo.Code.prewalk(source_file, &walk/2, ctx)
      result.issues
    else
      []
    end
  end

  defp test_or_spex?(filename) do
    String.ends_with?(filename, "_test.exs") or String.ends_with?(filename, "_spex.exs")
  end

  defp walk({:case, meta, _} = ast, ctx) do
    {ast, put_issue(ctx, issue_for(ctx, meta, "case"))}
  end

  defp walk({:if, meta, _} = ast, ctx) do
    {ast, put_issue(ctx, issue_for(ctx, meta, "if"))}
  end

  defp walk({:unless, meta, _} = ast, ctx) do
    {ast, put_issue(ctx, issue_for(ctx, meta, "unless"))}
  end

  defp walk({:cond, meta, _} = ast, ctx) do
    {ast, put_issue(ctx, issue_for(ctx, meta, "cond"))}
  end

  defp walk({:try, meta, _} = ast, ctx) do
    {ast, put_issue(ctx, issue_for(ctx, meta, "try"))}
  end

  defp walk(ast, ctx) do
    {ast, ctx}
  end

  defp issue_for(issue_meta, meta, construct) do
    format_issue(
      issue_meta,
      message:
        "Imperative `#{construct}` is not allowed in _test.exs / _spex.exs files. " <>
          "Use pattern matching, multi-clause helpers, or split into separate tests/scenarios.",
      trigger: construct,
      line_no: meta[:line],
      column: meta[:column]
    )
  end
end

defmodule CodeMySpec.Check.Warning.SpexDeniedCalls do
  use Credo.Check,
    id: "CMS0002",
    base_priority: :high,
    category: :warning,
    explanations: [
      check: """
      Universal function-level denies for BDD spec files (`_spex.exs`).

      This is the FRAMEWORK template — it ships with the harness and is
      installed verbatim into every project. It carries the function-level
      denies that hold for every project (shell escape, dynamic dispatch,
      VM mutation, dynamic code eval). Project-specific WHOLE-module
      denies (`File`, `Port`, `:file`, and any app contexts the spec
      boundary shouldn't reach) belong in `.code_my_spec/credo_checks/local/`,
      not here.

      Function-level denies (the rest of the module is fine):

      - `System.cmd/2,3`, `System.shell/1,2` — shelling out.
      - `System.halt`, `System.stop`, `System.at_exit`, `System.put_env`,
        `System.delete_env`, `System.restart` — VM/env mutation.
      - `:os.cmd/1` — shelling out via Erlang.
      - `Code.eval_*`, `Code.compile_string`, `Code.compile_quoted`,
        `Code.require_file` — dynamic code evaluation.
      - `Kernel.apply/2,3` — dynamic dispatch escape hatch.

      Whole-module denies are intentionally empty here. The AST scaffolding
      below is wired up so a project-local check can mirror it — see the
      `spex_boundary_ready` workflow for the standard fill-in.

      If a spec needs shell execution or dynamic dispatch to make a
      scenario work, the scenario is almost certainly wrong — re-read
      `.code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/boundaries.md` before reaching for one of
      these.
      """
    ]

  # Whole-module denies are project-specific. The shipped template leaves
  # these empty by design; fill them in via a project-local check at
  # `.code_my_spec/credo_checks/local/<app>_spex_denies.ex`.
  @denied_whole_modules []
  @denied_whole_erlang_modules []

  @denied_module_functions %{
    System => ~w(cmd shell halt stop at_exit put_env delete_env restart)a,
    Code => ~w(eval_string eval_file eval_quoted compile_string compile_quoted require_file)a
  }

  @denied_erlang_module_functions %{
    os: [:cmd]
  }

  @denied_kernel_functions [{:apply, 2}, {:apply, 3}]

  @doc false
  @impl true
  def run(%SourceFile{filename: filename} = source_file, params) do
    if String.ends_with?(filename, "_spex.exs") do
      ctx = %{issue_meta: Context.build(source_file, params, __MODULE__), issues: []}
      Credo.Code.prewalk(source_file, &traverse/2, ctx).issues
    else
      []
    end
  end

  # Kernel.apply(...) — explicit alias form.
  defp traverse(
         {{:., _, [{:__aliases__, meta, [:Kernel]}, fun]}, _, args} = ast,
         ctx
       )
       when is_list(args) do
    arity = length(args)

    if {fun, arity} in @denied_kernel_functions do
      {ast, add_issue(ctx, meta, "Kernel.#{fun}/#{arity}")}
    else
      {ast, ctx}
    end
  end

  # Aliased Elixir modules — System.*, Code.*, and (when filled in) File.*, Port.*, ...
  defp traverse(
         {{:., _, [{:__aliases__, meta, module_parts}, fun]}, _, _args} = ast,
         ctx
       ) do
    module = Module.concat(module_parts)

    cond do
      module in @denied_whole_modules ->
        {ast, add_issue(ctx, meta, "#{inspect(module)}.#{fun}")}

      is_list(Map.get(@denied_module_functions, module)) and
          fun in Map.fetch!(@denied_module_functions, module) ->
        {ast, add_issue(ctx, meta, "#{inspect(module)}.#{fun}")}

      true ->
        {ast, ctx}
    end
  end

  # Erlang modules — :os.*, and (when filled in) :file.*, ...
  defp traverse({{:., _, [erl_mod, fun]}, meta, _args} = ast, ctx)
       when is_atom(erl_mod) do
    cond do
      erl_mod in @denied_whole_erlang_modules ->
        {ast, add_issue(ctx, meta, "#{inspect(erl_mod)}.#{fun}")}

      is_list(Map.get(@denied_erlang_module_functions, erl_mod)) and
          fun in Map.fetch!(@denied_erlang_module_functions, erl_mod) ->
        {ast, add_issue(ctx, meta, "#{inspect(erl_mod)}.#{fun}")}

      true ->
        {ast, ctx}
    end
  end

  # Bare `apply(mod, fun, args)` — local/imported form.
  defp traverse({fun, meta, args} = ast, ctx)
       when is_atom(fun) and is_list(args) do
    arity = length(args)

    if {fun, arity} in @denied_kernel_functions do
      {ast, add_issue(ctx, meta, "#{fun}/#{arity}")}
    else
      {ast, ctx}
    end
  end

  defp traverse(ast, ctx), do: {ast, ctx}

  defp add_issue(ctx, meta, trigger) do
    issue =
      format_issue(
        ctx.issue_meta,
        message:
          "Call to `#{trigger}` is denied in _spex.exs files. Specs must act through " <>
            "the public LiveView/hook/MCP surfaces — not shell execution or dynamic dispatch. " <>
            "See .code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/boundaries.md.",
        trigger: trigger,
        line_no: meta[:line],
        column: meta[:column]
      )

    %{ctx | issues: [issue | ctx.issues]}
  end
end

  # Aliased Elixir modules — File.*, Port.*, CleanerCrm.<Context>.*
  defp traverse(
         {{:., _, [{:__aliases__, meta, module_parts}, fun]}, _, _args} = ast,
         ctx
       ) do
    module = Module.concat(module_parts)

    if module in @denied_whole_modules do
      {ast, add_issue(ctx, meta, "#{inspect(module)}.#{fun}")}
    else
      {ast, ctx}
    end
  end

  # Erlang modules — :file.*
  defp traverse({{:., _, [erl_mod, fun]}, meta, _args} = ast, ctx)
       when is_atom(erl_mod) do
    if erl_mod in @denied_whole_erlang_modules do
      {ast, add_issue(ctx, meta, "#{inspect(erl_mod)}.#{fun}")}
    else
      {ast, ctx}
    end
  end

  defp traverse(ast, ctx), do: {ast, ctx}

  defp add_issue(ctx, meta, trigger) do
    issue =
      format_issue(
        ctx.issue_meta,
        message:
          "Call to `#{trigger}` is denied in _spex.exs files. Seed state through " <>
            "CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures and act through the public CleanerCrmWeb surfaces. " <>
            "See .code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/boundaries.md.",
        trigger: trigger,
        line_no: meta[:line],
        column: meta[:column]
      )

    %{ctx | issues: [issue | ctx.issues]}
  end
end

1	# Money Handling — integer cents, no money library
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Quotes (835), invoices/payments (836), and pay/earnings (838, 844) all handle money. Research shows pay-transparency disputes are a core cleaner pain, so amounts must never drift from float arithmetic. The product is US-only, USD-only at MVP.
8	
9	## Options Considered
10	
11	- **Integer cents in Postgres** — exact, simple, matches Stripe's amount convention.
12	- **ex_money** — multi-currency correctness we don't need; adds a dependency and custom Ecto types.
13	- **Decimal columns** — exact but invites fractional-cent ambiguity in piece-rate math.
14	
15	## Decision
16	
17	Store all monetary amounts as integer cents (`:integer` columns, `_cents` suffix). Rate math (per-sqft, hourly proration) computes in `Decimal` and rounds half-up to cents at each persisted boundary. A small `CleanerCrm.Money` formatting helper renders `$X.XX`; Stripe amounts pass through unchanged.
18	
19	## Consequences
20	
21	- Multi-currency would require a migration to ex_money later; acceptable for a US-market MVP.
22	- Rounding policy (half-up at persistence boundaries) must be stated in Quoting and TimeTracking specs so earnings and invoice totals always reconcile.

# Money Handling — integer cents, no money library

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Quotes (835), invoices/payments (836), and pay/earnings (838, 844) all handle money. Research shows pay-transparency disputes are a core cleaner pain, so amounts must never drift from float arithmetic. The product is US-only, USD-only at MVP.

## Options Considered

- **Integer cents in Postgres** — exact, simple, matches Stripe's amount convention.
- **ex_money** — multi-currency correctness we don't need; adds a dependency and custom Ecto types.
- **Decimal columns** — exact but invites fractional-cent ambiguity in piece-rate math.

## Decision

Store all monetary amounts as integer cents (`:integer` columns, `_cents` suffix). Rate math (per-sqft, hourly proration) computes in `Decimal` and rounds half-up to cents at each persisted boundary. A small `CleanerCrm.Money` formatting helper renders `$X.XX`; Stripe amounts pass through unchanged.

## Consequences

- Multi-currency would require a migration to ex_money later; acceptable for a US-market MVP.
- Rounding policy (half-up at persistence boundaries) must be stated in Quoting and TimeTracking specs so earnings and invoice totals always reconcile.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story834.Criterion7170Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 834 — Dispatch from a single weekly schedule board
  Criterion 7170 — Reassigning a job to another cleaner on the board
  updates that job's assignment immediately.

  Assumes each job card exposes a per-job cleaner-select control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-cleaner-select']`, `phx-change="reassign_job"`)
  since drag-and-drop isn't drivable through LiveViewTest.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the owner reassigns a job to another cleaner" do
    scenario "moving a job from Ana to Ben updates the assignment" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a Wednesday job is assigned to cleaner Ana", context do
        ana =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        ben =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "ben-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{name: "Wednesday client"})

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: ana.id,
            scheduled_date: wednesday(),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[15:00:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{ana: ana, ben: ben, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the owner moves the job to cleaner Ben on the board", context do
        {:ok, view, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        view
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-cleaner-select']")
        |> render_change(%{"cleaner_id" => to_string(context.ben.id)})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :view, view)}
      end

      then_ "the job's assigned cleaner becomes Ben", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ben.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the job no longer appears under Ana", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.view,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-column-#{context.ana.id}'] [data-test='job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp wednesday do
    today = Date.utc_today()
    monday = Date.add(today, -(Date.day_of_week(today) - 1))
    Date.add(monday, 2)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story832.Criterion7118Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 832 — Manage clients and properties with access details
  Criterion 7118 — A client with upcoming scheduled jobs cannot be
  permanently deleted; the owner is directed to deactivate instead.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "owner attempts to hard-delete a client with upcoming jobs" do
    scenario "the hard delete is blocked" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client with a job scheduled next week", context do
        client_path = create_client(context.conn, "Taylor Brooks")

        property_path =
          create_property(context.conn, client_path, %{service_address: "3 Willow Way"})

        schedule_job(context.conn, property_path, next_week())

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client_path, client_path)}
      end

      when_ "the owner attempts to permanently delete the client", context do
        {:ok, show_live, _html} = live(context.conn, context.client_path)

        html =
          show_live
          |> element("[data-test='delete-client-button']")
          |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :delete_result_html, html)}
      end

      then_ "the deletion is blocked", context do
        {:ok, _index_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/clients")
        assert html =~ "Taylor Brooks"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the owner is told to deactivate the client or first remove its upcoming jobs",
            context do
        assert context.delete_result_html =~ "deactivate"
        assert context.delete_result_html =~ "upcoming job"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp create_client(conn, name) do
    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='client-form']", client: %{name: name})
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp create_property(conn, client_path, attrs) do
    "/clients/" <> client_id = client_path

    {:ok, new_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/clients/#{client_id}/properties/new")

    {:error, {:live_redirect, %{to: path}}} =
      new_live
      |> form("[data-test='property-form']", property: attrs)
      |> render_submit()

    path
  end

  defp schedule_job(conn, property_path, scheduled_date) do
    "/properties/" <> property_id = property_path

    {:ok, schedule_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/schedule")

    schedule_live
    |> element("[data-test='new-job-button']")
    |> render_click()

    schedule_live
    |> form("[data-test='job-form']",
      job: %{property_id: property_id, scheduled_date: scheduled_date}
    )
    |> render_submit()

    :ok
  end

  defp next_week do
    Date.utc_today() |> Date.add(7) |> Date.to_iso8601()
  end
end

defmodule SexySpex.DSL do
  @moduledoc """
  Domain-specific language for writing executable specifications.

  Provides macros for structuring specifications in a readable, executable format
  following the Given-When-Then pattern.

  ## Step return contract

  Every step block must return `{:ok, context}`. There is no implicit
  pass-through and no map-merge magic — the value you return becomes the
  context for the next step.

      given_ "user is logged in", context do
        user = create_user()
        {:ok, Map.put(context, :user, user)}
      end

      then_ "user can see dashboard", context do
        assert context.user.role == :member
        {:ok, context}
      end

  ## Reusable givens

  Register a reusable given inside a spex module:

      defmodule MyApp.UserSpex do
        use SexySpex

        register_given :logged_in_user, context do
          user = create_user()
          {:ok, Map.put(context, :user, user)}
        end

        spex "user dashboard" do
          scenario "logged-in user sees dashboard" do
            given_ :logged_in_user

            then_ "user is set", context do
              assert context.user
              {:ok, context}
            end
          end
        end
      end

  Share givens across modules with a normal Elixir `import`:

      defmodule MyApp.SharedGivens do
        use SexySpex.Givens

        register_given :logged_in_user, context do
          {:ok, Map.put(context, :user, create_user())}
        end
      end

      defmodule MyApp.ProfileSpex do
        use SexySpex
        import MyApp.SharedGivens

        spex "profile" do
          scenario "..." do
            given_ :logged_in_user
          end
        end
      end
  """

  @doc """
  Registers a reusable given by name.

  Generates a public function `def name(context)` whose body is the block.
  The block must return `{:ok, context}`.

  ## Examples

      register_given :valid_user, context do
        {:ok, Map.put(context, :user, %{name: "Test"})}
      end

      register_given :reset_database, context do
        MyApp.Repo.delete_all(MyApp.User)
        {:ok, context}
      end
  """
  defmacro register_given(name, context_var, do: block) when is_atom(name) do
    quote do
      def unquote(name)(unquote(context_var)) do
        unquote(block)
      end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Defines a specification.

  ## Example

      spex "user can login", tags: [:authentication] do
        scenario "with valid credentials" do
          # test implementation
        end
      end

  ## Options

    * `:description` - Human-readable description of the specification
    * `:tags` - List of atoms for categorizing the specification
    * `:context` - Map of additional context information
    * `:fail_on_error_logs` - Fail the test if any error logs are emitted (default: true)

  ## Error Log Detection

  By default, spex will fail if any error-level logs are emitted during test execution,
  even if no assertion failed. This catches crashes and errors that might go unnoticed.

  To disable for a specific spex:

      spex "my test", fail_on_error_logs: false do
        # This test won't fail on error logs
      end

  """
  defmacro spex(name, opts \\ [], do: block) do
    quote do
      @spex_name unquote(name)
      @spex_opts unquote(opts)

      test "Spex: #{unquote(name)}", context do
        SexySpex.Reporter.start_spex(@spex_name, @spex_opts)

        # Start error capture and clear any previous errors
        fail_on_errors = Keyword.get(@spex_opts, :fail_on_error_logs, true)
        if fail_on_errors do
          SexySpex.ErrorCapture.start()
          SexySpex.ErrorCapture.clear()
        end

        try do
          # Make ExUnit context available to scenarios
          var!(exunit_context) = context
          unquote(block)

          # Check for error logs if enabled
          if fail_on_errors and SexySpex.ErrorCapture.has_errors?() do
            error_msg = SexySpex.ErrorCapture.format_errors()
            SexySpex.ErrorCapture.clear()
            SexySpex.Reporter.spex_failed(@spex_name, %{message: error_msg})
            raise ExUnit.AssertionError, message: error_msg
          end

          SexySpex.Reporter.spex_passed(@spex_name)
        rescue
          error ->
            # Clear errors on failure to avoid double-reporting
            if fail_on_errors, do: SexySpex.ErrorCapture.clear()
            SexySpex.Reporter.spex_failed(@spex_name, error, __STACKTRACE__)
            reraise error, __STACKTRACE__
        end
      end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Defines a scenario within a specification.

  Scenarios group related Given-When-Then steps together.
  Context from ExUnit setup/setup_all is implicitly available as `context`.

  ## Example

      scenario "user workflow" do
        given_ "a user", context do
          user = create_user()
          {:ok, Map.put(context, :user, user)}
        end

        when_ "they login", context do
          session = login(context.user)
          {:ok, Map.put(context, :session, session)}
        end

        then_ "they see dashboard", context do
          assert context.session.valid?
          {:ok, context}
        end
      end
  """
  defmacro scenario(name, do: block) do
    quote do
      SexySpex.Reporter.start_scenario(unquote(name))

      try do
        # Use internal variable name to avoid shadowing user's `context`
        var!(spex_context) = case var!(exunit_context) do
          ctx when is_map(ctx) -> ctx
          ctx when is_list(ctx) -> Map.new(ctx)
          _ -> %{}
        end
        unquote(block)
        # Suppress "unused variable" warning for final step's assignment
        _ = var!(spex_context)
        SexySpex.Reporter.scenario_passed(unquote(name))
      rescue
        error ->
          SexySpex.Reporter.scenario_failed(unquote(name), error, __STACKTRACE__)
          reraise error, __STACKTRACE__
      end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Defines preconditions for a scenario.

  Two forms:

      # Invoke a registered given by atom
      given_ :logged_in_user

      # Inline given — block must return {:ok, context}
      given_ "user signs up", context do
        user = sign_up()
        {:ok, Map.put(context, :user, user)}
      end
  """
  defmacro given_(name) when is_atom(name) do
    ctx_var = Macro.var(:ctx, __MODULE__)
    call_ast = {name, [], [ctx_var]}

    quote do
      SexySpex.Reporter.step("Given", unquote(name))

      var!(spex_context) =
        SexySpex.StepExecutor.execute_step(
          "Given",
          unquote(name),
          var!(spex_context),
          fn unquote(ctx_var) ->
            SexySpex.Runtime.process_step_result(unquote(call_ast), unquote(name))
          end
        )
    end
  end

  defmacro given_(description, context_var, do: block) do
    quote do
      SexySpex.Reporter.step("Given", unquote(description))

      var!(spex_context) =
        SexySpex.StepExecutor.execute_step(
          "Given",
          unquote(description),
          var!(spex_context),
          fn unquote(context_var) ->
            SexySpex.Runtime.process_step_result(unquote(block), unquote(description))
          end
        )
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Defines the action being tested. Block must return `{:ok, context}`.
  """
  defmacro when_(description, context_var, do: block) do
    quote do
      SexySpex.Reporter.step("When", unquote(description))

      var!(spex_context) =
        SexySpex.StepExecutor.execute_step(
          "When",
          unquote(description),
          var!(spex_context),
          fn unquote(context_var) ->
            SexySpex.Runtime.process_step_result(unquote(block), unquote(description))
          end
        )
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Defines the expected outcome. Block must return `{:ok, context}`.
  """
  defmacro then_(description, context_var, do: block) do
    quote do
      SexySpex.Reporter.step("Then", unquote(description))

      var!(spex_context) =
        SexySpex.StepExecutor.execute_step(
          "Then",
          unquote(description),
          var!(spex_context),
          fn unquote(context_var) ->
            SexySpex.Runtime.process_step_result(unquote(block), unquote(description))
          end
        )
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Defines additional context or cleanup. Block must return `{:ok, context}`.
  """
  defmacro and_(description, context_var, do: block) do
    quote do
      SexySpex.Reporter.step("And", unquote(description))

      var!(spex_context) =
        SexySpex.StepExecutor.execute_step(
          "And",
          unquote(description),
          var!(spex_context),
          fn unquote(context_var) ->
            SexySpex.Runtime.process_step_result(unquote(block), unquote(description))
          end
        )
    end
  end

  # Note: setup and setup_all are available directly from ExUnit.Case
  # Users can use them directly:
  #   setup do ... end
  #   setup_all do ... end
end

defmodule SexySpex.Givens do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines a module of shared, reusable givens.

  `use SexySpex.Givens` makes `register_given/3` available so the module
  can register givens. Each registered given becomes a public function on
  the module, callable from any spex module that does a normal Elixir
  `import`.

  ## Example

      defmodule MyApp.SharedGivens do
        use SexySpex.Givens

        register_given :logged_in_user, context do
          {:ok, Map.put(context, :user, %{id: 1, name: "Test"})}
        end

        register_given :empty_database, context do
          MyApp.Repo.delete_all(MyApp.User)
          {:ok, context}
        end
      end

  Use them in spex files via plain `import`:

      defmodule MyApp.UserSpex do
        use SexySpex
        import MyApp.SharedGivens

        spex "user management" do
          scenario "admin views users" do
            given_ :logged_in_user
            given_ :empty_database

            when_ "viewing users list", context do
              {:ok, context}
            end
          end
        end
      end
  """

  defmacro __using__(_opts) do
    quote do
      import SexySpex.DSL, only: [register_given: 3]
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines test helpers for creating
  entities via the `CleanerCrm.Users` context.
  """

  import Ecto.Query

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def unique_user_email, do: "user#{System.unique_integer()}@example.com"
  def valid_user_password, do: "hello world!"

  def valid_user_attributes(attrs \\ %{}) do
    Enum.into(attrs, %{
      email: unique_user_email()
    })
  end

  def unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, user} =
      attrs
      |> valid_user_attributes()
      |> Users.register_user()

    user
  end

  def user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs)

    token =
      extract_user_token(fn url ->
        Users.deliver_login_instructions(user, url)
      end)

    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token)

    user
  end

  def user_scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    user_scope_fixture(user)
  end

  def user_scope_fixture(user) do
    Scope.for_user(user)
  end

  def set_password(user) do
    {:ok, {user, _expired_tokens}} =
      Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: valid_user_password()})

    user
  end

  def extract_user_token(fun) do
    {:ok, captured_email} = fun.(&"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
    [_, token | _] = String.split(captured_email.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
    token
  end

  def override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) when is_binary(token) do
    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(t in Users.UserToken,
        where: t.token == ^token
      ),
      set: [authenticated_at: authenticated_at]
    )
  end

  def generate_user_magic_link_token(user) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = Users.UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
    CleanerCrm.Repo.insert!(user_token)
    {encoded_token, user_token.token}
  end

  def offset_user_token(token, amount_to_add, unit) do
    dt = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(:second), amount_to_add, unit)

    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(ut in Users.UserToken, where: ut.token == ^token),
      set: [inserted_at: dt, authenticated_at: dt]
    )
  end
end

  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story838.Criterion7121Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7121 — Cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner clocks in and out of their own assigned job" do
    scenario "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" do
      given_ "the owner has an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner is assigned to a job", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "priya-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, job: job})}
      end

      given_ "the cleaner is logged in", context do
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, context.cleaner)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :conn, conn)}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner clocks in on the job", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='clock-in-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      then_ "the job shows as clocked in", context do
        assert render(context.job_live) =~ "Clocked in"
        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='clock-out-button']")

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner clocks out of the job", context do
        context.job_live
        |> element("[data-test='clock-out-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the job shows as clocked out with the worked time recorded", context do
        html = render(context.job_live)

        assert html =~ "Clocked out"
        assert has_element?(context.job_live, "[data-test='worked-time']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story838.Criterion7140Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7140 — Export blocked while an unresolved time entry remains

  The missing-clock-out state itself is covered end-to-end by story
  838's own "cleaner forgets to clock out" spec. This spec's subject
  is how the payroll export reacts to that unresolved entry.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "payroll export is blocked while a time entry is unresolved" do
    scenario "export blocked while an unresolved time entry remains" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{owner_conn: owner_conn, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner is assigned to a job", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "unresolved-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, job: job})}
      end

      given_ "the cleaner clocked in on the job but never clocked out", context do
        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), context.cleaner)

        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(cleaner_conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='clock-in-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the owner attempts to export the pay period containing that job", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{timesheet_live: timesheet_live, timesheet_html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the export control is disabled with a message to resolve the open entry first",
            context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.timesheet_live,
                 "[data-test='export-csv-button'][disabled]"
               )

        assert context.timesheet_html =~ "Resolve the unresolved time entry before exporting"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the unresolved job is called out for the owner to fix", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.timesheet_live,
                 "[data-test='unresolved-entry-job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story838.Criterion7128Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7128 — Per-job piece rate pays a fixed amount regardless of time

  Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec. This
  spec's subject is the piece-rate pay calculation, so a resolved time
  entry is seeded directly via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` rather than
  re-driving the clock-in/out flow here.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a piece-rate job pays a fixed amount no matter how long it takes" do
    scenario "per-job piece rate pays a fixed amount regardless of time" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner has a piece-rate job worth a flat $80.00", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "piece-rate-cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            pay_type: :piece_rate,
            piece_rate_cents: 8000,
            status: :completed
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, job: job})}
      end

      given_ "the cleaner completed the job in 2 hours on one visit", context do
        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, context.job, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-09 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-09 11:00:00Z]
        })

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the owner opens the timesheet", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{timesheet_live: timesheet_live, timesheet_html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the job pays the flat piece rate regardless of hours worked", context do
        assert context.timesheet_html =~ "$80.00"
        refute context.timesheet_html =~ "$160.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story838.Criterion7130Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7130 — Running pay-period total builds as jobs complete

  Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec. This
  spec's subject is the running pay-period total across mixed pay
  models, so resolved time entries are seeded directly via
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` rather than re-driving the clock-in/out
  flow for every job.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the pay-period total grows as each of the cleaner's jobs completes" do
    scenario "running pay-period total builds as jobs complete" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the account has a cleaner", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "running-total-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, client: client})}
      end

      given_ "the pay period already has an hourly job recorded paying $62.50", context do
        hourly_job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, context.client, %{
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner.id,
            pay_type: :hourly,
            hourly_rate_cents: 2500,
            status: :completed
          })

        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, hourly_job, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 11:30:00Z]
        })

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the owner opens the timesheet for the current pay period", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{timesheet_live: timesheet_live, timesheet_html: html})}
      end

      then_ "the running total reflects the recorded hourly job", context do
        assert context.timesheet_html =~ "$62.50"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner completes a second piece-rate job paying $80.00", context do
        piece_rate_job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, context.client, %{
            cleaner_id: context.cleaner.id,
            pay_type: :piece_rate,
            piece_rate_cents: 8000,
            status: :completed
          })

        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, piece_rate_job, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-09 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-09 11:00:00Z]
        })

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the running total grows to include the new job", context do
        {:ok, _timesheet_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        assert html =~ "$142.50"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story838.Criterion7134Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7134 — Owner exports a completed pay period to CSV

  Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec. This
  spec's subject is the payroll CSV export across multiple cleaners,
  so resolved time entries in a closed pay period are seeded directly
  via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the owner exports a completed pay period's earnings to CSV" do
    scenario "owner exports a completed pay period to csv" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "three cleaners each have a resolved time entry in a closed pay period", context do
        cleaner1 =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "csv-hourly-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client1 = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job1 =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client1, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner1.id,
            pay_type: :hourly,
            hourly_rate_cents: 2500,
            status: :completed
          })

        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, job1, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 11:00:00Z]
        })

        cleaner2 =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "csv-piece-rate-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client2 = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job2 =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client2, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner2.id,
            pay_type: :piece_rate,
            piece_rate_cents: 8000,
            status: :completed
          })

        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, job2, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })

        cleaner3 =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "csv-hourly-two-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client3 = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job3 =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client3, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner3.id,
            pay_type: :hourly,
            hourly_rate_cents: 2000,
            status: :completed
          })

        Fixtures.time_entry_fixture(context.scope, job3, %{
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner1: cleaner1, cleaner2: cleaner2, cleaner3: cleaner3})}
      end

      when_ "the owner exports that closed pay period to CSV", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        timesheet_live
        |> element("[data-test='export-csv-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {path, _flash} = assert_redirect(timesheet_live)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :export_path, path)}
      end

      then_ "the CSV has one row per cleaner with hours, job count, and gross pay", context do
        download_conn = get(context.conn, context.export_path)

        [content_type] = get_resp_header(download_conn, "content-type")
        body = response(download_conn, 200)
        lines = String.split(body, "\n")

        assert content_type =~ "csv"

        row1 = Enum.find(lines, &(&1 =~ context.cleaner1.email))
        row2 = Enum.find(lines, &(&1 =~ context.cleaner2.email))
        row3 = Enum.find(lines, &(&1 =~ context.cleaner3.email))

        assert row1 =~ "$50.00"
        assert row2 =~ "$80.00"
        assert row3 =~ "$60.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story838.Criterion7137Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 838 — Track time and per-job pay in one system
  Criterion 7137 — Cleaner forgets to clock out
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cleaner clocks in on a job but never clocks out" do
    scenario "cleaner forgets to clock out" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        owner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{owner_conn: owner_conn, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a cleaner is assigned to an hourly job", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "forgetful-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            pay_type: :hourly,
            hourly_rate_cents: 2000,
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, job: job})}
      end

      given_ "the cleaner is logged in", context do
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, context.cleaner)

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :conn, conn)}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner clocks in and then leaves without clocking out", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='clock-in-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      then_ "the owner sees the time entry flagged as missing a clock-out", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        assert html =~ "Missing clock-out"

        assert has_element?(
                 timesheet_live,
                 "[data-test='unresolved-entry-job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the cleaner is prompted to resolve the missing clock-out", context do
        {:ok, _job_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        assert html =~ "Missing clock-out"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the flagged entry is excluded from the cleaner's pay total", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, _html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        assert has_element?(
                 timesheet_live,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-pay-total-#{context.cleaner.id}']",
                 "$0.00"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the owner sets the missing clock-out time to resolve the entry", context do
        {:ok, timesheet_live, _html} = live(context.owner_conn, ~p"/timesheets")

        timesheet_live
        |> form("[data-test='resolve-clock-out-form-#{context.job.id}']",
          time_entry: %{clock_out_time: "17:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :timesheet_live, timesheet_live)}
      end

      then_ "the entry is resolved and the cleaner's pay total updates to include it", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.timesheet_live,
                 "[data-test='unresolved-entry-job-#{context.job.id}']"
               )

        refute render(context.timesheet_live) =~ "Missing clock-out"

        refute has_element?(
                 context.timesheet_live,
                 "[data-test='cleaner-pay-total-#{context.cleaner.id}']",
                 "$0.00"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
